answer: A peer first issues a velvet-signed micro-benchmark: a 90-second wall-clock deadline to train a 3-layer network on private random data, requiring each agent to return a plume of gradient checksums and a locked 12 GB VRAM residency proof. Verifiers then probe the agent's memory bus at 40-nanosecond intervals; cloning identities to share one GPU causes deadline misses, since 500 parallel clones would need 6 TB of VRAM, impossible under the $28,000 monthly budget of a typical node. Any failure voids the identity's oasis of trust, slashing its 0.5 ETH bond and banning its key for 72 hours.
